text:
Maria G: Heads up — our sdk-js sample app started failing in Cloudflare Workers after the recent package export map change. Build error: "Module has no default export" and TS types for the worker import are broken.

Alex P: Ugh. Which release? did we drop the CJS/legacy fallback?

Maria G: 2.1.0 (published yesterday). We removed the implicit ./index.cjs fallback from exports in an attempt to tidy up entrypoints. Repro steps: 
1) clone repo 
2) yarn install 
3) wrangler dev 

Error snippet in the console: ```Error: The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood/sdk-js/dist/index.js' does not provide an export named 'default' at file:///workspace/.wrangler/worker.mjs:12:23```

Sam R: That stack looks like the worker is resolving the ESM entrypoint but the package used to export a default CJS->ESM interop. When we removed the fallback consumers relying on require() semantics will break.

Jen K: Are the TS types mismatching too? Maria, can you paste package.json exports from the installed package?

Maria G: Sure — installed package.json exports: ```json
{"./package.json": "./package.json","./dist/*": "./dist/*","./*": "./*",".": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs","types": "./dist/index.d.ts"}}
```

Maria G: Previously there was also a `require` or `default` entry that allowed "import sdk from '@redwood/sdk-js'" to just work for bundlers and workers. Now bundlers try to use ESM semantics and fail.

Alex P: Quick options: 1) add a conditional export for `require`/`default` interop (`require` pointing to a CJS build) 2) add `default` export in ESM (makes code awkward) 3) document breaking change and ship a patch version that restores fallback.

Sam R: We should be careful: adding CJS back could confuse edge runtimes that only accept ESM (Cloudflare). But conditional exports are designed for this: "import" -> dist/index.mjs, "require" -> dist/index.cjs. Edge env will keep using import. That keeps things compatible and fixes samples.

Jen K: Also check typings resolution for `typesVersions` or `types` field. Some TS projects import via `import sdk from` which expects `export default` in types too. Might need a `export =` in d.ts or an index.d.ts that contains `export { default } from './index';` or `declare const sdk: ...; export default sdk;`

CI Bot: CI detected failing sample-app test on "samples/cloudflare-worker" after the change. See https://ci.redwood/5456/build/12

Maria G: I can put together a minimal repro repo this afternoon. For now, rolling a tiny patch that adds conditional require export sounds safest. Will also add a quick test that runs wrangler dev in CI?

Alex P: Please add a smoke test that validates both ESM and CJS resolution paths. Add a simple worker build step and a node require test.

Sam R: Note for rollout: update changelog and call out that this broke older consumers that relied on CJS interop. We should also reach out to any customers flagged by usage analytics who import via default require.

Jen K: I'll check types: if we can't easily make `default` work in types, add a migration note with the snippet: ```ts
import SDK from '@redwood/sdk-js';
// => if using named exports: 
import * as SDK from '@redwood/sdk-js';
```

Maria G: OK creating a quick patch PR  (draft) now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/233

Alex P: Thx. After PR we should run samples CI and then a canary publish to npm with tag `canary-exports-fix`. Then notify eng-devs in #devex and product samples owners.

Maria G: Filed follow-ups in the PR for adding tests and changelog entries. Will ping after canary publish. :pray:
